title: Terraform module for internal ingress: NLB/ALB with TLS termination and health checks
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Create a reusable Terraform module to provision internal ingress for Private (VPC) deployments. The module should support both AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) and Application Load Balancer (ALB) patterns, enable TLS termination (ALB) or TLS passthrough (NLB), and wire up robust health checks for Redwood services. This module will be used by Private/VPC customers and the on-prem packaging to standardize ingress, simplify upgrades, and make observability consistent across deployments.

Scope and goals:
- Support internal (non-internet-facing) load balancers inside customer VPCs and private subnets.
- Provide option to choose ALB (layer 7) or NLB (layer 4) per environment.
- ALB must support TLS termination with ACM or customer-supplied certs; ALB should support path-based routing to route /api, /health, and websocket routes.
- NLB must support TLS passthrough as well as TLS termination via TLS listeners for customers who prefer it.
- Health checks configurable per target group: path, interval, healthy/unhealthy thresholds, success codes. Defaults should match Redwood runtime probes (GET /_internal/health returns 200).
- Expose outputs for target group ARNs, LB DNS name (internal), listener ARNs, security group IDs, and the module should emit tags and audit-friendly metadata.
- Support optional internal TLS certificate provisioning via ACM Private CA or accept an existing certificate ARN stored in KMS-backed secrets.
- Include upgrade strategy notes for in-place replacement vs blue/green for critical listener/target changes.
- Provide examples for single-AZ dev, multi-AZ prod, and on-prem equivalents with annotations for metal load balancer adapters.

Constraints and non-goals:
- Only AWS implementation in scope for this ticket; GCP/Azure to follow in separate work.
- This module should not manage DNS records in customer zones, but should optionally emit the LB endpoints for DNS automation consumers.
- No changes to runtime application code; assume apps expose configurable health endpoints.

Risks and considerations:
- ALB rule changes can cause short-lived connection resets; document rollback and maintenance window requirements.
- Certificate rotation needs careful handling for zero-downtime: provide guidance and an example workflow using ACM certificate re-association.
- NLB with TLS passthrough requires target instances to terminate TLS; ensure KMS/HSM keys are available in those environments.
- Cross-account/private-link patterns may require additional IAM and endpoint configurations; flag as advanced config.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a boolean to select load balancer type: use_nlb = true|false
ALB option creates internal ALB, listener on 443 with TLS termination, and path-based routing for /api and /health
NLB option creates internal NLB with TCP or TLS listener and optional TLS passthrough
Default health checks point to GET /_internal/health and can be overridden per target group
Module outputs target group ARNs, listener ARNs, LB internal DNS name, and security group IDs
Certificate can be provided via certificate_arn input or auto-provisioned using acm_certificate_arn with integration notes
Terraform plan for changing listeners shows safe defaults and a documented upgrade procedure to avoid client disruption
Unit/integration example in examples/ shows single-AZ dev and multi-AZ prod layouts and passes basic curl health checks in CI
